sentences.text: This dinosaur is estimated to have reached lengths between 11 and 12.2 meters, with a mass ranging from 4 to 4.6 tons.
Known only from postcranial bones, it possessed a more gracile build compared to other massive theropods like Tyrannosaurus.
The genus name merges the formation name Baharia with the Greek word for lizard, while the species name means huge.
Richard Markgraf unearthed the fossils in April 1914 at Gebel Ghorabi near Ain Gedid, Egypt, before they were moved to Munich.
Ernst Stromer formally described the genus and species B. ingens in 1934 based on finds from the Bahariya Formation.
The original specimens were destroyed during World War II bombings, though additional remains were later discovered in Agadez, Niger.
Historically placed in Carcharodontosauridae and Tyrannosauroidea, its taxonomic position is now thought to belong in Noasauridae.
Bahariasaurus lived during the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous, with its fossil record spanning from the Albian to the Maastrichtian stages.
It inhabited the wetland environment of the Bahariya Formation alongside Tameryraptor and Spinosaurus.
The attribution of fossils from Niger is debated, with some suggesting they belong to a carcharodontosaurid, while others hypothesize Bahariasaurus is a juvenile Deltadromeus.
